items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The regulars were Maycoks, Cocksey, Edgar James and myself.

ctx.x: I was taking a small taste and the others were taking a deep breath before they drank and therefore they could take a large taste in their mouths before they swallowed it. I soon caught on the trick so well that it was seldom that they asked me to take the poison off and I became one of the best alley drinking musicians in town. We would go in some alley or back yard to drink after we had bought the whisky.

I began to get some gigs with these musicians who were mostly free lancers and did not care too much to have a regular job. Most of them as I said before were 35 years old or more and I was the youngest in the bunch so they called me "the Kid." There was Edgar James, a fat drummer, Wilbur Coksey, an alto player from the West Indies, a pianist named Maycoks, and a few other musicians that came around now and then. But the regulars were Maycoks, Cocksey, Edgar James and myself.

The first job I did with these new found friends was a one-week gig in the lobby of the Pekin Theatre which was a movie house owned by a real American Indian. I knew the son of the owner of this theatre before I started playing music. There was a certain film that was showing for a week which was a rarity because the movie houses usually changed films every other day. We were engaged to play a few numbers, 2 or 3 at the end of each showing of this film and I really enjoyed the week.
